prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] `landing/index.html`: single-file page on Mondrian's 1930 work, using only FACTSHEET.md.

[action] I wrote one file with inline CSS and no JavaScript.
- **Layout:** a CSS grid of cells separated by thick black lines. The colours are red, blue and yellow on off-white.
- **Cells:** title; red cell with "1930" and "Oil on canvas"; painter; movement; collection; the Neoplastic rules; an SVG schematic of the composition; the "why it matters" line; and a call to action linking to the fact sheet's Wikipedia source.
- **Font:** Archivo from Google Fonts, with Helvetica and Arial as fallback.
- **Three.js:** left out. The 2D grid carries the idea, and the CDN is an extra failure point.

Assumptions:
- Only fact-sheet content appears. That includes the alternate title, 1917 founding by van Doesburg and Mondrian, Kunsthaus Zurich, and the principles.
- I treated the SVG as a schematic of the described layout, not a copy of the painting. The footer says so. Its proportions are my own and are not claimed to be exact.
- The page has a mobile breakpoint and a visible focus style on the link.

[result] The file exists at 6180 bytes. I have not opened it in a browser, so the layout and the Google Fonts load are not verified. What I can say is that every factual line was checked against the fact sheet by eye. The only external requests are Google Fonts and the Wikipedia link.

[next] Open `landing/index.html` and check the grid at desktop and phone widths.
